name: Khotanese
notes: STUB — no grapheme inventory modelled. Khotanese (Khotanese Saka), an Eastern Middle Iranian language of the Buddhist kingdom of Khotan on the southern Silk Road (Tarim Basin, modern Hotan, Xinjiang), attested in Buddhist and administrative manuscripts from roughly the 5th-10th centuries CE. It is written in a variant of the Brahmi abugida (South Turkestan Brahmi) adapted from an Indic model to Iranian phonology, with a complex and still-debated vowel/consonant value system (the script's Indic vowel signs and virama conventions do not map cleanly onto Khotanese's own phonemic inventory, and reconstructions of exact sound values remain contested among specialists, e.g. Emmerick vs. later revisions). No single, uncontroversial letter-to-IPA table is available from the sources consulted, so this spec is an honest stub rather than a guessed inventory. Added so it resolves as an ancestry/contact node for the Saka/Khotanese-Tumshuqese subgroup of Eastern Iranian.
